name: Bun Kabab
description: Pakistani street-style bun kabab with hot shami kabab, egg, chutneys, onion and chaat masala in a lightly toasted bun.
ingredients: Cooking oil, for frying and toasting
method: Heat a little oil in a pan and shallow-fry the prepared shami kababs until hot through and browned on both sides.
Season the beaten eggs lightly if desired, pour into the pan and cook as a thin omelette; divide it among the four buns or coat the kababs in egg according to your preferred bun-kabab style.
Split the buns and toast the cut sides lightly on the pan so they are warm without becoming hard.
Spread green chutney and tamarind chutney over the toasted buns, adjusting the sweet, sour and spicy balance to taste.
Place a hot kabab and egg in each bun, then add sliced onion and a light sprinkle of chaat masala.
Close the buns and serve immediately while the kabab is hot and the bread is still lightly crisp at the edges.
image_alt: Pakistani bun kabab with hot shami patty, egg, chutneys, onion and a lightly toasted bun
image_caption: Street-style bun kabab assembled with a hot shami kabab, egg, green and tamarind chutneys and onion.
technique: Treat bun kabab as an assembly dish with three timing-sensitive parts: a hot shami kabab, just-cooked egg and a bun toasted only enough to give structure. Build it immediately so chutneys do not soak through the bread before serving.
doneness_cues: Shami kabab should be hot through and browned on both sides.
Egg should have no liquid raw areas remaining.
The bun cut surface should be lightly toasted but still soft enough to bite easily.
Chutneys should coat the bun without pooling heavily at the bottom.
mistakes: Toasting buns until dry and hard.
Adding a large amount of watery chutney too early and making the bun soggy.
Assembling with a cold centre because the shami kabab was only browned outside.
Overloading chaat masala so the sandwich becomes salty.
substitutions: Use homemade or prepared shami kababs, but heat them fully before assembly.
Egg can be cooked as a thin omelette or used to coat the kabab depending on preferred street style.
Adjust green versus tamarind chutney to control spicy versus sweet-sour balance.
storage: Store buns, chutneys and cooked filling components separately if preparing ahead. A fully assembled bun kabab softens quickly.
reheating: Reheat the shami kabab separately in a pan until hot, then toast the bun fresh and assemble with cold chutneys and onion.
serving: Serve immediately after assembly, with extra chutney on the side rather than soaking the bun.

faqs.question: Why does bun kabab get soggy?
faqs.answer: Watery chutney, untoasted bread and long holding after assembly are the main causes. Toast lightly and assemble only when ready to serve.

faqs.question: Should the egg be inside or around the kabab?
faqs.answer: Both styles are used. This recipe supports a thin omelette or an egg-coated patty.

faqs.question: Can I assemble bun kababs ahead?
faqs.answer: It is better to prepare the components ahead and assemble at serving so the bun stays pleasant.
